back: A project moves the organization from a current state to a future state, sometimes through a transition state.
A structured approach for transitioning individuals, groups and organizations to a future state where benefits are realized.
Change management helps people adopt; change control approves or rejects changes to documents, deliverables, baselines.
An internal EEF: vision, values, norms, leadership styles, hierarchy, ethics and codes of conduct.
From highly predictive plans to Lean Startup, where everything is an experiment.
Discuss priorities with stakeholders, team and management; place them on sliding scales; choose fitting techniques.
Exploration–execution, speed–stability, quantity–quality, flexibility–predictability.
Willing executives, willingness to change how people are assessed, suitable centralization, balanced goals, mature talent management.
Silos, short-term procurement pricing, rewards for local efficiency, narrow specialists, too many projects per person.
Mutual trust and full clarity on roles, responsibilities, agreements and processes.
Accelerated delivery; shifts in ways of working.
Market pressure, compliance mandates, technology and operating model shifts, closing value gaps.
Check alignment and value, sponsors and stakeholders, resources and risks, the plan (via change control), readiness to adopt.
Formulate, plan, implement change; manage transition; sustain change; with feedback loops.
Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, Reinforcement.
Urgency, coalition, vision, communicate, remove obstacles, short-term wins, build on change, anchor in culture.
Late status quo, foreign element, chaos, transforming idea, practice and integration, new status quo.
Change is situational, transition psychological: ending, neutral zone, new beginning.
Motivational, not forceful: engagement and two-way communication; address valid concerns.
Too many changes too fast cause resistance and fatigue; pace change to the change appetite.
Activities after implementation so people do not return to the old state.
Visible executive sponsorship, communication and coaching, progressive pacing, incremental introduction, leading by example.
A backlog of changes, each tried as an experiment, tracked on a kanban board.
Change lead time, adoption rate, throughput.

front: Change management as a value enabler
back: Drives adoption, outcomes and benefits realization; from strategic planning into operations.
